response.sql:
WITH linked AS (
  SELECT s.signalregistry, s.modindex, s.phaseshiftdeg, t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile
  FROM signals s
  JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
  JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(modindex) AS base_mod FROM linked
),
groups AS (
  SELECT telescregistry, weathprofile, AVG(modindex) AS grp_mod, AVG(phaseshiftdeg) AS grp_phase
  FROM linked
  GROUP BY telescregistry, weathprofile
),
kept AS (
  SELECT g.* FROM groups g CROSS JOIN baseline b WHERE g.grp_mod > b.base_mod
)
SELECT k.weathprofile,
  AVG(k.grp_mod) AS avg_mod_index,
  AVG(k.grp_phase) AS avg_phase_shift,
  AVG(k.grp_mod - b.base_mod) AS avg_mod_above_baseline
FROM kept k CROSS JOIN baseline b
GROUP BY k.weathprofile;

assumptions.assumption: Linking uses inner joins, so signals whose telescref has no matching telescope, or whose telescope's observstation has no matching observatory, are dropped.
The baseline is AVG(modindex) over every linked signal, with NULL modulation indexes ignored, so each signal counts equally. It is not an average of the telescope/weather group averages.
Group averages use AVG, which ignores NULL modindex and phaseshiftdeg values. A group with no non-null modindex has a NULL average and is dropped by the comparison.
A NULL weathprofile is treated as its own weather group, so it appears as a NULL row in the output. The request does not say whether observatories with missing weather data should be excluded.

The 'average amount above baseline' is the average of (group average modindex minus baseline) over the kept groups. This equals the average group modindex minus the baseline, and no rounding is applied.
